pattern.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
pattern.description: People with low competence overestimate their ability, while experts underestimate theirs.
pattern.mechanism: The less you know, the more confident you are. The more you know, the more you see what you don't know.

cross_domain_matches.question: Where might the Dunning-Kruger effect be strongest in The One Group? What are people overconfident about?

pattern.name: Information Arbitrage
pattern.description: Profiting from price differences of the same asset in different markets. In knowledge, profiting from knowing something others don't.
pattern.mechanism: Find where information is unevenly distributed and exploit the gap.
signals: Same concept priced differently in different contexts
Knowledge that doesn't cross industry boundaries

cross_domain_matches.question: What information arbitrage exists in The One Group? What do you know that others don't?

pattern.name: Meta Shift
pattern.description: The 'meta' (most effective tactics available) shifts when someone discovers a new strategy that beats the current best.
pattern.mechanism: The optimal strategy changes when someone innovates, making old strategies obsolete.

cross_domain_matches.question: What if the meta in The One Group is about to shift? What new strategy would make current best practices obsolete?

pattern.name: Red Queen Effect
pattern.description: In evolutionary systems, you must keep running just to stay in place. Competitors co-evolve, so advantages are temporary.
pattern.mechanism: Continuous adaptation is required just to maintain position, not to gain ground.

cross_domain_matches.question: In The One Group, you're running just to stay in place. What if your competitors are adapting faster than you're innovating?

pattern.name: Niche Specialization
pattern.description: Species that occupy narrow niches face less competition but are vulnerable to niche destruction.
pattern.mechanism: Specialization reduces competition but increases extinction risk.

cross_domain_matches.question: Is The One Group too specialized? What happens if the niche shrinks or disappears?

pattern.name: Asymmetric Warfare
pattern.description: A weaker opponent can defeat a stronger one by avoiding their strengths and attacking their weaknesses.
pattern.mechanism: Don't play the game the leader wants you to play. Change the battlefield.
signals: Leader investing in defending their strength

cross_domain_matches.question: What would asymmetric warfare look like against the leaders in The One Group? Where are they weakest?

pattern.name: Flanking Maneuver
pattern.description: Instead of attacking the strongest point, go around it and attack from an unexpected direction.
pattern.mechanism: Find the angle the opponent isn't defending and attack there.

cross_domain_matches.question: What flanking maneuver would catch everyone in The One Group off guard?

pattern.name: Supply Line Vulnerability
pattern.description: An army's greatest vulnerability is its supply line. Cut it and the army collapses regardless of its strength.
pattern.mechanism: Identify what the opponent needs to function and target that.

cross_domain_matches.question: What's the supply line vulnerability in The One Group? What single point of failure would collapse the system?

pattern.name: Long Tail Risk
pattern.description: Rare, high-impact events that models underestimate because they haven't happened recently.
pattern.mechanism: The most important risks are the ones that haven't materialized yet.

cross_domain_matches.question: What long-tail risk is everyone in The One Group ignoring because it hasn't happened recently?

pattern.name: Compound Effects
pattern.description: Small advantages compound over time into massive differences. The key is consistency and time horizon.
pattern.mechanism: Small, consistent edges become insurmountable advantages given enough time.
